method: Deterministic summary of computed figures. No language model is used.
national: One Nation led national search interest in the week to 8 November, averaging 32.0 on Google's 0-100 scale, 5.0 times the next party (Labor). That is 68% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
One Nation rose the most on the previous week, up 6.3 points (+24%).

Searches for One Nation jumped to 56 on 3 November, 2.1 times the previous week's average. Coverage around that day: “One Nation volunteer allegedly beaten with bat after dispute over signage” (ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation).
Fastest-rising searches alongside One Nation: “mike newman”, “one nation superannuation policy”, “one nation immigration policy dispute”.
victoria: 18 days until Victorians vote on Saturday 28 November 2026.

Across the latest poll from each of 6 pollsters, the Coalition averages 31.4% of the primary vote, Labor 22.2%, One Nation 20.5% and the Greens 14.2%. On two-party-preferred the Coalition leads 55.2 to 44.8 (4 polls), a 10.2-point swing to the Coalition since 2022.
Applied uniformly to the 2022 pendulum, that swing points to a Coalition majority (59 seats, 45 needed). Treat this as the classic two-party read only: it cannot see One Nation winning seats.
The Roy Morgan MRP (March 2026 - September 2026), which models seats one by one, projects Coalition 62, Labor 40, One Nation 11 and Greens 6: a majority.
Preferred premier (Resolve, 2–7 Nov 2026): Wilson 35%, Carroll 21%, Pickering 15%.

One Nation led Victorian search interest in the week to 8 November, averaging 59.1 on Google's 0-100 scale, 6.2 times the next party (the Liberals). That is 69% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
Among the leaders, search interest ran Wilson 70%, Carroll 22%, Pickering 7%, Sandell 1% of the combined total this week.
